proposed_assessment.route: PD166285 / kinase-inhibition-mediated meiotic progression after EML1 depletion
proposed_assessment.disposition: Retain partial cell-cycle-state rescue comparator; faithful division, fertility and MVA rescue remain unestablished
proposed_assessment.rationale: At 10 µM, PD166285 accelerates meiotic entry and suppresses aberrant pronucleus formation after EML1 depletion. Native Figure 9 shows modest normal-spindle improvement only with delayed treatment; continuous treatment is nonsignificant for that endpoint and most treated oocytes remain abnormal. No normal drug-treated control or drug-specific BUBR1, chromosome-count or fertility outcome is supplied. The tested product is a dihydrochloride with broad kinase activity, not established selective WEE1/2 inhibition. Lower pY15-CDK1 supports pathway action without isolating the target. Delayed treatment duration conflicts between caption and graph.
